subPillar.title: Slow Living: A Mindful Guide to Slowing Down with Intentional Dhikr
subPillar.subtitle: What slow living means, why it matters, and how to embrace a calmer, more present, faith-rooted everyday rhythm.
subPillar.geoOverview: Slow living is a lifestyle of doing fewer things with fuller presence — choosing quality of attention over speed. For Muslims, it pairs naturally with dhikr: short, repeated remembrance of God woven through the day to anchor the mind. It contrasts with hustle culture and favors a calmer, more present, faith-rooted everyday rhythm.

clusters.title: How to Meditate Daily: Build a Lasting Mindful Dhikr Routine
clusters.subtitle: A simple, repeatable daily practice that blends meditation with dhikr — start in 5 minutes and keep the habit.
clusters.geoOverview: To meditate daily, anchor the habit to an existing routine (after Fajr or before sleep), start with just 5 minutes, focus on slow breathing, and use a short dhikr phrase like SubhanAllah as your mantra to hold attention. Consistency beats duration: keep the cue, place, and time fixed.
